rgb: This is an outdoor dirt yard, with flat rows and columns of molded clay bricks bearing the stamp 'SUV' spread across the ground ahead of the camera wearer from approximately 0.5 metres to 5 metres away. A vertical wall of stacked bricks borders the left side at about 0.5 to 1.5 metres away. At the bottom foreground, within arm's reach (0.3 to 0.6 metres away), both of the wearer's hands hold a rectangular brick mold over the dirt floor. Near the upper edge, roughly 4 to 5 metres ahead, part of a bicycle and the lower legs of a distant person standing next to it can be seen. During frames 1 and 2, the wearer gazes down over the brick grid while the mold sits on the ground at the bottom edge, partially cut off, and the stacked-brick wall continues along the upper left. In frame 3, the view angles farther downward and moves closer to the ground as both hands raise and flip the mold about 0.4 metres in front of the wearer. This releases a new brick at the front of the left-most ground column in frame 4, while the hands pull the mold back toward the bottom edge. By frame 5, the wearer turns their head and gaze to the right and slightly upward, causing the left-side brick wall and the wearer's hands to leave the view entirely, while open dirt on the right and the bicycle's lower wheels with the nearby person's feet enter view at the top-left.
depth: The depth map depicts an outdoor ground plane extending from around 0.4 m away in the lower foreground to approximately 3–5 m at the top. On the far left is a vertical brick stack 0.6–1.5 m away, while flat rows of bricks stamped 'SUV' cover the ground ahead and to the right. In frames 1 through 4, the camera wearer's hands and the brick being held are the brightest foreground features, positioned within arm's reach (0.3–0.6 m away), below the wearer's head and in front of the ground-level rows. They remain low in frames 1–2, rise slightly toward the center-left row in frame 3 and block the ground behind them, descend again in frame 4, then vanish beneath the image in frame 5 when the camera rotates right and tilts slightly upward. The resulting view shows rows extending from 0.5–4 m away and a distant bicycle at ~4 m in the upper left. Unlike the consistently brown, dirt-coated RGB views, the depth representation distinctly separates the raised foreground brick and arms from the rows underneath and emphasizes the height transitions between the upright stack at left and the level grid at right. Nevertheless, it handles the low relief of the individual ground bricks poorly, flattening them into nearly uniform gradients, and incorrectly saturates frame 5's lower foreground as an excessively bright white area even though that region contains only flat sandy ground.
segmentation: Across the five frames, the segmentation map is nearly all blank. It identifies nothing in frames 1, 2, and 4, even though the scene contains a dense field of ground bricks 0.5–4 m away, an upright brick stack on the left 0.6–1.5 m away, and the camera wearer's hands with a held brick within arm's reach at 0.3–0.6 m. In frame 3, the system labels the wearer's right hand and forearm at the bottom center—about 0.4 m away and entering the image from below—as 'person'. It marks the held brick immediately above that hand, approximately 0.5 m away, as 'book', while calling an upper-left area of sandy soil and stacked bricks 0.6–1.2 m away a 'sandwich'. When the camera swings rightward in frame 5, it labels a partly shown bicycle together with a person's lower legs at the top-left boundary as 'bicycle'. These are roughly 3.5–4.5 m away, around 2–3 m beyond the closest brick rows, and the person/bicycle is oriented approximately sideways and severely clipped by the upper border. Although the map draws sharp boundary outlines around the held brick and right forearm in frame 3 and exposes the small, easily missed bicycle along frame 5's top edge, its overall performance is very unreliable: it omits nearly every scene component, does not segment the left arm in frame 3, and wrongly identifies bricks and dirt as a book and a sandwich.
pose: Frames 1 to 4 of the pose map are entirely black, with no detection of the camera wearer's own extended forearms and hands as they hold and place bricks 0.3–0.6 m away along the bottom of the image. Frame 3 also produces no magenta hand skeletons or yellow arm keypoints, despite both left and right hands and wrists being plainly visible in the foreground while gripping opposite ends of a brick, with the hands separated by about 0.3 m. Frame 5 contains a small, knotted grouping of yellow body keypoints close to the top-left boundary, approximately 3.5–4.5 m ahead of the camera wearer and behind the laid brick field. It corresponds to the feet and lower legs of a distant person standing next to a bicycle, while the person's upper body is cut off above the image. Since the view includes only the lower legs and feet, and the estimated skeleton compresses into a horizontal tangle beside the bicycle wheels, the map cannot dependably show the distant person's facing direction or establish whether they are looking at the camera wearer. The pose output is therefore unreliable for both the nearby egocentric hands and the severely cropped figure farther away.
